steps.text: Some materials carry heat quickly (conductors), others slow it down (insulators). Let's race them.
Tap “Start Race!” and watch the heat travel up each material.
The metal wins — heat races through it. Wood and plastic lag far behind; they're insulators.
Conductors (metals) let heat through fast; insulators (wood, plastic, air) block it. That's why cooking pots are metal but their handles aren't.

coach.mission: Race the materials to see which conducts heat fastest.
whenStuck: Tap “Start Race!” and watch which material heats up first.
Compare a metal with wood or plastic.
whenWrong: Metals conduct fast (win); wood and plastic are insulators (slow).
If it lagged behind, that material is an insulator.
whenCorrect: Right — the metal conducted heat fastest.
Good — insulators like wood block heat.
coach.done: You've raced conductors against insulators. Try Compare mode, or move on when you're ready.
